key_insight: An automated NCCT radiomics system can segment intracerebral hemorrhage and combine imaging, clinical, and demographic data to predict outcome more accurately than conventional assessment alone.
clinical_relevance: If validated in practice, this type of explainable decision-support tool could help clinicians stratify spontaneous ICH prognosis earlier and more precisely using routine admission CT scans.
method: Deep-learning hematoma segmentation on noncontrast CT.
Extracted 1,690 radiomics features and reduced them to 42 reproducible predictors to build a Rad-score.
Combined the Rad-score with clinical/demographic variables in machine-learning models for outcome prediction and prognostic stratification.
evidence_signal: The study used 2,680 patients across training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, and reported strong performance gains, including R² improving from 0.35 to 0.93 for functional outcome prediction when radiomics was added.
watch_item: This is a retrospective multicenter model, so real-world performance, workflow integration, and generalizability still need prospective validation before routine use.
paper_title: An automated, explainable, NCCT-based clinical decision-support system for spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage.
